title: Israel and Hamas reach a Gaza ceasefire and hostage release agreement
body:
On 15 January 2025, Israel and Hamas reached an agreement on a ceasefire in Gaza and the release of hostages, announced after indirect talks in Doha, Qatar, facilitated by the United States, Egypt and Qatar. Envoys of both the outgoing Biden administration and the incoming Trump team pressed the parties. Qatar's prime minister said the ceasefire was due to begin on Sunday 19 January.

The deal had three phases. In the six-week first phase there would be a full ceasefire, Israeli withdrawal from populated areas of Gaza, the release of hostages including women, the elderly and the wounded, releases of Palestinian prisoners, and a surge in humanitarian aid. Hamas agreed to release 33 Israeli hostages, and a Palestinian official estimated that about 1,000 Palestinians would be released from Israeli custody. In phase two, male soldiers held hostage would be released, remaining Israeli forces would withdraw and the ceasefire would become permanent. In phase three the remains of deceased hostages would be returned and reconstruction would begin.

The agreement required formal approval by Israel's cabinet, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said several unresolved points remained. President Joe Biden said the deal matched a May 2024 proposal endorsed by the UN Security Council, and President-elect Donald Trump said on social media that the hostages would be released shortly.
